Join us in resisting the Q4 doldrums by celebrating the designers, builders, and thinkers leading a system override. From stories on the power of thinking small, to the ways AI and prototyping are poised to help us smash through old workflows, it’s the toolkit you need to build better.

#### [Small but mighty](#small-but-mighty)

“You can make a bigger positive impact by focusing on the little actions users take most often than by adding a seemingly flashy feature that they don’t use,” says Sho Kuwamoto, Vice President of Product. We sat down with Sho to learn why shipping improvements and bug fixes aimed at quality of life is a foundational ritual at Figma. Whether it’s saving time or anticipating a need, creating a great product experience comes down to the details.

[![An illustration of a pixelated smiley face](data:image/png;base64,)![An illustration of a pixelated smiley face](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/6cb9805fdc067cd5c0bab7caeb4df7b58e375b61-696x914.png?w=528&h=693&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/little-big-updates-2023/)

#### [Breaking barriers with AI](#breaking-barriers-with-ai)

Zooming out and panning over, we check in with the product team to learn why and how they brought generative AI into FigJam. “At Figma, when we talk about lowering the floor and raising the ceiling, we mean creating products that are more accessible but also expand what’s possible,” says Noah Levin, Vice President of Product Design. Our new AI-powered features generate custom templates and diagrams, summarize content, and sort stickies, making it easier for everyone on a product team to plan, sync, and brainstorm together.

[![An illustration of abstracted UX elements on a lavender background](data:image/png;base64,)![An illustration of abstracted UX elements on a lavender background](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/5ac7f3156d11ec307c7761b8a031bef0e709fc63-860x860.png?w=528&h=528&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/introducing-ai-to-figjam/)

#### [Prototyping culture](#prototyping-culture)

Prototyping offers more than a final flourish—it’s an indispensable step in the many stages of product development. After all, prototypes concretize a design concept for collaborators to explore, react to, and refine. Prototyping gives designers more agency and empowers the entire team with better insights. Here’s how it can streamline your process and supercharge your efficiency.

[**Read more**](https://www.figma.com/blog/why-cultivating-a-prototyping-culture-will-help-you-build-better-products/)

#### [Calling all creators](#calling-all-creators)

What do a pair of digital googly eyes, a line of cascading text, and a code-generating plugin all have in common? They were made with the help of the Creator Fund, our grant program supporting free widgets, plugins, and files made by and for the [Figma Community](https://www.figma.com/community). Check out some of the amazing resources created by our first cohort of grant recipients and learn how you can apply to jump-start your next project.

#### [Rabbit hole](#rabbit-hole)

Illustrations by Laura Simonati and Jay Daniel Wright

![A collage including a poster for the 1944 film "Gaslight," an illustration showing a polka-dot briefcase reading "69%" and an illustration of a person sitting on a desk chair holding up binoculars that read 2024](data:image/png;base64,)![A collage including a poster for the 1944 film "Gaslight," an illustration showing a polka-dot briefcase reading "69%" and an illustration of a person sitting on a desk chair holding up binoculars that read 2024](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/4de6fe2a75f9816c80fe58c932b9df8bccdaeff3-1300x730.png?rect=0,1,1300,729&w=804&h=451&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

1\. A New Year’s resolution from coach and strategist Sara Wachter-Boettcher: Instead of trying to prove your worth as a designer, [let the work speak for itself](https://medium.com/nice-work-from-active-voice/hey-designers-theyre-gaslighting-you-e02e5a4d9cff).

2\. It’s a tactic to continue the upward trend. According to our new report, [69% of designers feel their job prospects have improved](https://www.figma.com/blog/state-of-the-designer-report-23/)

and are happier in their roles.

3\. Speaking of happiness—learn how to fall (back) in love with tech, pick up new work lingo, chart a career pivot, and more in [Figma’s 2023 Handoff](https://www.figma.com/blog/figma-2023-handoff/)

.
